gloss: shoji paper; paper for sliding screens

definitions.explanation: Thin, translucent white paper used to cover the wooden lattice frames of shoji sliding doors. It allows soft, diffused light to pass through while providing privacy.

examples.japanese: {障子紙|しょうじがみ}を{張|は}り{替|か}えた。
{子供|こども}が{障子紙|しょうじがみ}に{穴|あな}を{開|あ}けてしまった。
examples.english: The child poked a hole in the shoji paper.

examples.japanese: {年末|ねんまつ}の{大掃除|おおそうじ}で{障子紙|しょうじがみ}を{新|あたら}しくするのが{毎年|まいとし}の{恒例|こうれい}だ。
examples.english: Replacing the shoji paper during the year-end cleaning is an annual tradition.

notes:
CULTURE:
Shoji paper is traditionally replaced at least once a year, often during the year-end cleaning ({大掃除|おおそうじ}). The old paper is peeled off, the frame is cleaned, and fresh paper is pasted on. Modern alternatives include plastic-reinforced shoji paper that is more durable.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {障子紙|しょうじがみ}を{張|は}る (to paste shoji paper)
- {障子紙|しょうじがみ}を{張|は}り{替|か}える (to replace shoji paper)
- {障子紙|しょうじがみ}が{破|やぶ}れる (the shoji paper tears)
